title: Token Counter – Count Tokens in Files and Text | OpenAnyDoc
description: Count the tokens, words and characters in a PDF, Word, PowerPoint, Excel, CSV or JSON file, or in pasted text, before you paste it into an AI chat.
heading: Token Counter
subtitle: See how many tokens a file or text uses before you paste it into an AI chat; nothing is uploaded.
intro: Check whether a document will fit in an AI chat before you paste it into ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini. Drop a PDF, Word, PowerPoint, Excel, CSV, JSON, TXT or Markdown file, or paste text, and see its tokens, words and characters. Files are first turned into text the way the AI-ready converters do it: a PDF's or Word document's text, a deck's slide outline, tables as Markdown. Tokens are counted with a standard tokenizer, the same one GPT-4o models use; other models split text their own way, so for them the count is an estimate. Everything is counted in your browser and nothing is uploaded.

faq.question: Is my text uploaded?
faq.answer: No. Files are read and counted by your own browser, on your device. Pasted text stays in this tab and is never sent anywhere, not to a server and not to any AI service. Nothing is saved on the site: no share links and no history.

faq.question: What is a token?
faq.answer: A piece of text that an AI model reads as one unit: often a whole short word, part of a longer word, or a punctuation mark. Chat limits and prices are counted in tokens, not words.

faq.question: Is the count exact for ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini?
faq.answer: It is counted with a standard tokenizer, the same one GPT-4o models use. Claude, Gemini and other models use their own tokenizers, so for them the number is an estimate that is usually close but not exact.

faq.question: Why does my PDF show 0 tokens?
faq.answer: It is probably scanned: its pages are pictures, so there is no text to count. OCR PDF adds a text layer, then you can count it here.

faq.question: Why do Arabic texts use more tokens?
faq.answer: Tokenizers learn from text, and most of that text is English, so Arabic words are often split into more pieces. The same meaning in Arabic can take more tokens than in English.

faq.question: How can I make a file use fewer tokens?
faq.answer: Paste only the part you need, and for data try JSON to TOON, which writes lists of records in a shorter form.

faq.question: How do I count the tokens in a PDF or Word file?
faq.answer: Turn the file into plain text and run it through a tokenizer, the tool an AI model uses to split text into tokens. In OpenAnyDoc, drop the PDF, Word or other file and its tokens, words and characters appear at once, counted in your browser without uploading the file.
